title: Whether to build an Organizational Morphogenesis Layer now
problem: UNIIMENTE lacks one verified durable cross-organ mission closure, while dynamic organization is more complex and has not defeated the conventional durable workflow. The decision is whether to build a new runtime, do nothing, or stage the smallest falsifiable OMNIMORPH experiment through canonical seams.
baseline: The merged Event Spine and DurableWorkflow provide explicit durable state; DALEOBANKS uses fixed scheduled jobs; WealthMachine uses a fixed specialist roster and in-memory flow; StandingCognitionRuntime is proposal-only; no verified cross-organ closure exists.

alternatives.name: Static durable workflow
alternatives.description: Encode the mission as a fixed canonical DurableWorkflow with independent evaluation and no topology adaptation.
alternatives.revival_evidence: This remains the default and wins whenever dynamic candidates fail to produce a material advantage.

alternatives.name: Centralized coordinator
alternatives.description: A bounded coordinator decomposes and synthesizes while workers execute leased tasks.
alternatives.revival_evidence: Measured low task volume, high coupling and latency sensitivity outperform the static baseline.

alternatives.name: Decentralized task fabric
alternatives.description: Workers claim independent tasks from canonical queues without a permanent master.
alternatives.revival_evidence: A sealed high-volume low-coupling corpus shows a verified advantage after coordination cost.

alternatives.name: Hierarchical organization
alternatives.description: Bounded local coordinators recursively decompose specialist domains without inheriting or minting authority.
alternatives.revival_evidence: Recursive decomposition materially improves quality or latency while supervisor load and amplification stay within frozen thresholds.

alternatives.name: Hybrid organization
alternatives.description: Central mission coherence, decentralized bounded execution and structurally independent evaluation.
alternatives.revival_evidence: The preregistered experiment demonstrates a hard-dimension advantage without evidence, authority or maintainability regression.

alternatives.name: Developmental local organization
alternatives.description: Locally interacting components adapt organization from local evidence and thresholds.
alternatives.revival_evidence: It first defeats both static workflow and simpler dynamic forms under preregistered failures.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: Preserve current runtimes and avoid added complexity, but leave organizational choice implicit and the durable closure bottleneck unresolved.

roles.position: Preserve the institutional-compiler objective but refuse authority expansion and agent-hierarchy substitution.
material_concerns: Competing implementations and dissent must survive

roles.position: Place shared semantics in contracts and organizational composition in OMNIMORPH; reuse Event Spine and Consequence Gate.
Dynamic topology has not earned promotion; static durable workflow is the protected strongest competitor.
Accept only Phase-1 contracts and preregistration now; defer runtime until the owner is decided.
material_concerns: Rollback must be deletion of an inert experiment

roles.position: Require independent evaluation, dissent preservation, participant-welfare guardrails and executed episodes before knowledge promotion.
material_concerns: Participant harm hidden by aggregate optimization

evidence.claim: The repository already has a canonical durable event/workflow substrate.
evidence.reference: uniimente-kernel events/README.md and events/spine.py at PR #87 head
evidence.finding: Event Spine, inbox/outbox and DurableWorkflow own durable state; the spine does not confer authority.

evidence.claim: OMNIMORPH already owns bounded composition and retirement without self-activation.
evidence.finding: Composition, simulation, exact Gate receipt recording and accountable retirement are tested.
CVO=0, HARDENED=0 and whole-body closure remains false.

counterevidence.claim: Conventional durable workflow is currently stronger than developmental organization.
counterevidence.finding: Explicit state, targeted retry, low amplification and simpler supervision remain the evidence-backed default.

counterevidence.claim: Multi-agent deliberation did not economically defeat deterministic rules.
counterevidence.finding: V1 tied quality at roughly ten times modeled cost; V2 preserved dissent but still did not beat deterministic rules on the authored corpus.

counterevidence.claim: Prior developmental gates and semantic restoration failed.
counterevidence.finding: Failed runs are preserved and bar claims of developmental superiority.

pass_1.intended_outcome: Create the smallest reversible substrate that can test whether problem geometry predicts a materially better organization while the static workflow remains the default.

advantages.statement: Expands the option space without replacing the durable substrate.
advantages.amplified_value: Every candidate targets one Event Spine and one workflow truth source.

advantages.statement: Makes topology choice inspectable rather than prompt intuition.
advantages.amplified_value: Problem geometry, scorecards and episode refs become machine-checkable.
Schemas prohibit authority minting, inherited authority, evaluator suppression and Gate bypass.

advantages.statement: Turns losing structures into useful institutional evidence.
advantages.amplified_value: TopologyEpisode preserves losers, dissent, failure and costs instead of deleting them.
Verified mission-to-geometry-to-topology history can improve selection, sizing and evaluator placement across organs.

disadvantages.statement: The contract surface can become bureaucracy before runtime value exists.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Limit this PR to three contracts, one frozen experiment and no runtime.

disadvantages.statement: Dynamic candidates can disguise a permanent master-worker hierarchy.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Model coordinators as bounded rights with no authority minting and preserve do-not-instantiate/static forms.

disadvantages.statement: Topology selection can overfit a small authored corpus.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Seal held-out cases and thresholds before execution; retain results as hypotheses until repeated episodes.

disadvantages.statement: A second runtime or ownership conflict could fragment the Kernel.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Do not implement Phase 2 until PR #70/#87 runtime ownership receives an explicit decision.

disadvantages.statement: Coordination cost may erase any specialization or recovery benefit.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Preregister amplification/cost thresholds and make static workflow the automatic fallback.

comparisons.baseline: Current scheduled/in-memory organ flows plus the Kernel's conventional DurableWorkflow.
comparisons.do_nothing: Avoids new surface but cannot learn or falsify organizational selection and leaves VDM closure at zero.
comparisons.simplest_viable_alternative: One fixed static DurableWorkflow with independent evaluation; it is the default and protected fallback.
comparisons.strongest_competing_architecture: The conventional durable workflow, not a developmental topology.
comparisons.reversible_experiment: Freeze MissionContract, OrchestrationGenome, TopologyEpisode and a sealed five-phenotype internal comparison before any runtime integration.

rejected_alternatives.name: New orchestration package
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Duplicates canonical ownership and risks a second control plane.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Only a founder-ratified ownership decision proving no current owner can contain the semantics.

rejected_alternatives.name: Permanent master-agent hierarchy
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Concentrates design, execution and evaluation and fails the invention criterion.

rejected_alternatives.name: Immediate organ migration
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Jumps phases before contracts, baseline and runtime ownership are settled.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Phase-4 executed evidence and explicit Phase-5 integration decision.

pass_2.attack_summary: The strengthened proposal was attacked for bureaucracy, centralization, fragility, overfit, expense, vendor/model dependency, topology thrashing, evaluator capture, authority leakage, evidence theater, gaming, incomprehensibility and failure amplification. The result remains an inert experiment, not a runtime build.

new_weaknesses.statement: Large genomes may become impossible for operators to audit.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Require fail-closed schemas, content digests, a bounded phenotype set and human-readable scorecards.

new_weaknesses.statement: A topology could optimize one headline metric while harming evidence or participants.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Use hard constitutional invariants plus a multidimensional acceptance test and participant-welfare guardrail.

new_weaknesses.statement: Model/provider-specific evidence could become false institutional advantage.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Make provider eligibility plural/open and record provider composition in every episode.

new_weaknesses.statement: The compiler could become the practical authority even if schemas say otherwise.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: The compiler may emit hypotheses only; mission and consequence authority remain external references and human/Gate decisions.

new_weaknesses.statement: Reconfiguration during active tasks can corrupt state or amplify failure.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Prohibit live self-rewrite; require versioned proposals, bounded change, state-transfer proof and static rollback in later phases.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: The PR is capped at three schemas, tests and preregistration; no runtime or organ migration.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any proposal to add a fourth Phase-1 contract or executor.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Authority minting, inheritance, evaluator suppression and mission rewrite are schema-invalid.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any schema or code attempts to relax a constant-false invariant.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Overfit can only be decided by sealed held-out execution and repetition.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Held-out corpus is sealed before Phase 4.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: No Phase-2 runtime code will be written until ownership is explicitly decided.
Coordination overhead is a measured acceptance dimension; the static baseline wins ties.

pass_2.final_design: Phase 1 adds only fail-closed MissionContract, OrchestrationGenome and executed-only TopologyEpisode semantics under canonical owners; freezes a static-workflow-first comparative experiment; records ownership as proposed; leaves execution, task leases, reconfiguration and organ migration deferred. Five powers remain separate, and no model output can promote a genome without executed episode references.

residual_risks.mitigation: Block Phase 2 and stack this inert PR on #87 without editing runtime/.

residual_risks.risk: Schemas cannot enforce every relational constraint, such as worker maxima or identity inequality.
residual_risks.mitigation: Add a single canonical semantic validator in Phase 2 only after ownership is decided.

residual_risks.risk: The held-out corpus and acceptance thresholds are not yet independently sealed.
residual_risks.mitigation: Keep all topology claims at hypothesis/experiment-candidate status.

dissent.handling: The conventional durable workflow remains the protected default, strongest competitor and fallback. A tie with added complexity is a loss for the dynamic form.

entries.position: Do not promote organizational morphogenesis; the static durable workflow currently wins available evidence.
entries.rationale: PR #66/#68 and PumpStation V1/V2 show explicit-state/simple forms are more reliable or cheaper on the evidence available.
entries.evidence_threshold: At least one sealed mission geometry where a dynamic phenotype meets all invariants, matches quality and materially improves a hard dimension net of coordination cost, followed by a repeat run.

migration_plan: No migration in Phase 1. After an explicit runtime-ownership ruling, Phase 2 may adapt the existing Event Spine/DurableWorkflow through narrow contracts; Phase 4 runs in sandbox; Phase 5 integrates only an earned winner; organ migration remains later and separately gated.

steps: Close the draft PR without merge if ownership or contract semantics are rejected.
If merged later, revert only the three schemas, their tests and linked documentation before any consumer depends on them.
Retain the deliberation, failed evidence and reason for rollback as historical artifacts.
Continue using the existing static DurableWorkflow and current organ baselines.

kill_criteria: A second Event Spine, workflow truth source, authority system, identity system, Consequence Gate or Capability Genome system appears.
A topology can create authority, transfer supervisor authority to a worker, suppress a required evaluator or bypass consequence mediation.
The experiment cannot use actual canonical DALEOBANKS and WealthMachine interfaces.
A dynamic topology ties or loses after coordination cost while adding material complexity.
Restart duplicates consequential work or an uncertain external effect is retried without reconciliation.
Mission lineage is incomplete, dissolution leaves obligations, or model output is represented as executed evidence.
review_trigger: Alfonso rules on Phase-1 ownership/contracts, then a new linked decision is opened before Phase 2; no silent third strengthening pass is permitted.
